target_definition.metric: United States monthly PCE price change

graph_diagnosis.summary: Labor conditions, income-supported demand, and services-versus-goods price pressure form a reusable framework for monthly PCE inflation.
weaknesses: The direct PCE release and its downstream resolution link are excluded.
The available evidence is concentrated in a single retrospective release.

search_factors.why_search: Labor conditions can support confidence, income, and consumption.
Income-supported spending is a demand channel for price pressure.
Services can provide persistent upward pressure in the aggregate price index.
Goods and energy moves can offset services-led pressure.

checkpoints.mechanism: A resilient labor market can support household confidence and spending.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Labor indicators and household-demand data point in the same direction.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Labor conditions weaken while spending slows.

checkpoints.mechanism: Income-supported spending can increase demand-side price pressure.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Income and outlays remain mutually reinforcing.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Income gains are saved rather than spent.

checkpoints.mechanism: Persistent demand can amplify broad inflation pressure.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Spending strength aligns with broad price-pressure indicators.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Demand remains firm but price pressure eases broadly.

checkpoints.mechanism: Services price pressure can sustain broader inflation when demand is resilient.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Services measures remain firmer than offsetting components.

checkpoints.mechanism: Goods and energy declines can offset services-led aggregate price pressure.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Offsetting components are broad enough to matter for the aggregate.

checkpoints.mechanism: Demand-sensitive services pressure and offsetting goods and energy moves combine in the monthly PCE price change.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Reconcile services, goods, energy, income, and outlays in the component data.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Component movements do not reconcile with the aggregate index.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Resilient labor conditions can support income and spending, adding to aggregate price pressure.
applicability_conditions: Household demand remains responsive to income.
failure_conditions: Households retrench or savings absorb income gains.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Services pressure can be offset by disinflation in goods and energy when components are aggregated.
applicability_conditions: Offsetting components have material index weights.
failure_conditions: Services and offsetting components move in the same direction.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Goods and energy disinflation outweighs resilient services demand.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare weighted component contributions with income and outlays growth.

forecast_audit_questions: Do labor conditions, income, and outlays point to sustained demand?
Is services pressure broad enough to dominate the aggregate?
Are goods and energy declines large enough to offset services pressure?
Do component contributions reconcile with the monthly index?
